aliases.name: Steyr-Hahn
aliases.note: Hahn is German for hammer, and distinguishes it from the hammerless Roth-Steyr M1907.

aliases.name: Steyr M1911
aliases.note: The commercial name it was sold under before military adoption.

aliases.name: Steyr Repetierpistole M1912/P16
aliases.note: The selective-fire version with an extended magazine and a fitted stock.

massEmpty.sourceNote: 1.2 kg, credited in the infobox to Jane's. The magazine is integral, so an empty-versus-loaded distinction does not arise the way it does on a pistol with a detachable one.

barrelLength.sourceNote: 128 mm, which is also the test barrel length the published 9x23mm Steyr ballistics were measured in.

productionTotal.sourceNote: The infobox gives "up to 300,000", which is a ceiling rather than a count, so the figure is recorded as an estimate.

capacity.sourceNote: Integral eight-round magazine in the grip, filled from above with a stripper clip.
German rework. The magazine and its capacity are unchanged.

images.alt: A blued semi-automatic pistol on a grey ground, seen from the left. The slide is short and sits in a cut-out at the rear of a long one-piece frame; an external hammer stands at the back. The grip carries chequered wooden panels. Markings on the frame read Md.1912 under a crown, and STEYR 1913 on the slide.
images.caption: A Steyr M1912 built in 1913 on a Romanian contract, chambered in 9x23mm Steyr. The crown over "Md.1912" is the Romanian acceptance mark; the slide covers only the rear third of the frame, which is what gives the pistol its distinctive outline.

images.alt: A Steyr M1912 pistol lying on weathered grey planks, seen from the right, beside a green cardboard ammunition packet in German and a metal charger clip holding eight brass cartridges with round-nosed bullets.
images.caption: A 1915-made Steyr-Hahn with a period packet of 9 mm Steyr ammunition and a loaded eight-round charger. The clip is the only way the pistol is loaded: the magazine is part of the frame and cannot be taken out.
